title: Cenobamate (Xcopri) — titration and NPO options

maintenance.doseText: Adults: 12.5 mg once daily wk 1–2; 25 mg wk 3–4; 50 mg wk 5–6; 100 mg wk 7–8; 150 mg wk 9–10; 200 mg once daily from wk 11. If needed ↑ by 50 mg every 2 weeks to max 400 mg once daily. Don't exceed this schedule
notes: Faster titration risks serious adverse reactions incl. DRESS (§2.2, §5.1)

renalNotes: Mild–moderate (CLcr 30 to <90 mL/min) and severe (<30 mL/min): use with caution; dose reduction may be considered (§8.6)
hepatic: Baseline ALT, AST and total bilirubin before starting if none within 3 months (§2.1)
Mild–moderate (Child-Pugh A–B): max 200 mg once daily; further reduction may be considered (§2.3, §8.7)
enteral: Tablets may be crushed, mixed with 25 mL water and given by mouth or NG tube; flush with 10 mL water; confirm no particles remain (§2.4)
Crushed tablets by mouth or NG tube: Cmax and AUC similar to whole tablets; median Tmax 0.5 h (§12.3)
levels: 10–35 mcg/mL — AES 2024 summary Table 1 (range from AES Treatments Committee clinical experience, not the label)
interactions: Phenytoin: up to 2-fold ↑ — gradually ↓ phenytoin dose by up to 50% during titration (§7.1, Table 5)
Phenobarbital and N-desmethylclobazam ↑ — consider reducing phenobarbital or clobazam (Table 5)
Lamotrigine and carbamazepine ↓ — increase as needed (Table 5)
CYP2C19 substrates ↑ (consider reducing); CYP2B6 and CYP3A substrates ↓ (increase as needed) (Table 5)
Drugs that shorten QT: use caution (§7.2)
pearls: Contraindicated in familial short QT syndrome (§4)
DRESS, incl. one death, with weekly or faster titration; none in 1339 patients started at 12.5 mg and titrated every 2 weeks (§5.1)
Taper over ≥2 weeks unless safety requires abrupt stop (§2.5)
sources: Xcopri (cenobamate) tablets US prescribing information. SK Life Science; revised 8/2025 (user-supplied label)

Vossler DG, Gidal BE; American Epilepsy Society Treatments Committee. A Summary of Antiseizure Medications Available in the United States, 4th edition. American Epilepsy Society; revised April 1, 2024 (user-supplied)
